ambiguities.description: Enrollment and Grade Recording: The transcript states 'a student receives a letter grade for each course offering they were enrolled in' (line 31), which implies that whenever a student is enrolled in an offering, they must receive a grade. However, it is unclear whether every enrollment automatically results in a grade, or if there are scenarios (e.g., student withdrawal) where an enrolled student does not receive a grade. Should the model enforce a subset constraint: 'the Student-Offering pairs in the enrollment relationship must be a subset of those in the grading relationship'? Or is the reverse true (every graded pair must have an enrollment)?

source_references.excerpt: At the end of a semester, a student receives a letter grade for each course offering they were enrolled in.

ambiguities.description: Enrollment Optionality: While the transcript clearly states that students enroll in offerings (line 3), it does not explicitly state whether every student must enroll in at least one offering, or whether every offering must have at least one enrolled student. Should enrollment be mandatory in either direction?

source_references.excerpt: Students enroll in course offerings, not in courses directly.

ambiguities.description: Instructor Teaching Multiple Offerings: The transcript states 'An instructor can teach several offerings in the same semester' (line 11). This clarifies that an instructor can teach multiple offerings, but it does not explicitly rule out teaching the same offering multiple times (redundant) or whether an instructor must teach at least one offering. Should teaching be mandatory for instructors?

source_references.excerpt: An instructor can teach several offerings in the same semester.

ambiguities.description: Multiple Course Instances with Same Title/Credits: The transcript allows the same course code (e.g., CS101) to be offered in multiple semesters (line 7: 'Intro to Databases might run in both Fall and Spring'). However, it does not state whether a course's title or credit value can change over time. Should the model assume these are immutable properties of the course, or could they change and require historical tracking?

source_references.excerpt: Intro to Databases might run in both Fall and Spring.

ambiguities.description: Credit Value Constraint Precision: Line 19 states that the credit value is 'usually between 1 and 6', but does not confirm whether 1 and 6 are hard boundaries or merely typical. Could a course have 0 credits or 7+ credits in exceptional cases?

source_references.excerpt: The credit value is a whole number, usually between 1 and 6.
